views.name: users_basic_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation
FROM users

params.description: A one-row-per-user projection of basic profile attributes (Id, DisplayName, Reputation).
params.when_to_use: Lookup a user's display name and reputation by user Id | Join user identifying attributes onto other result sets as a dimension (one row per user) | Compose into larger queries that need user-level attributes without changing user-level cardinality
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier, derived directly from users.Id | DisplayName: the user's display name, derived directly from users.DisplayName | Reputation: the user's reputation score (integer), derived directly from users.Reputation
params.grounded_columns: users.Id | users.DisplayName | users.Reputation
params.metric: Id = users.Id | DisplayName = users.DisplayName | Reputation = users.Reputation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact/event tables or other one-row-per-user dimension views on users_basic_profile.Id = <other>.UserId (or equivalent) — safe because users_basic_profile is one-row-per-Id so joining on the user key does not duplicate these attributes. | do NOT join users_basic_profile to tables or views that are one-to-many to users (for example posts, comments, votes) without aggregation on the many-side first, because such joins will multiply rows and thereby duplicate the Reputation/DisplayName values. Instead aggregate the many-side (COUNT, SUM, etc.) grouped by the user key and then join the aggregated result to users_basic_profile. | If you need to combine this view with another user-level view that is also one-row-per-user, join on Id = Id directly — measures remain at user grain. | If you need to compute metrics that depend on counts from related tables (e.g., number of posts per user), compute those metrics in a subquery or CTE grouped by the related table's user key, producing one row per user, then join that result to users_basic_profile on Id to avoid duplicating Reputation.

views.name: posts_by_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId
FROM posts

params.description: Answers who owns each post and basic per-post attributes (score, view count, creation date, post type) at the post Id grain.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve attributes for a specific post or set of posts by Id (e.g., show post details for display or reporting). | Aggregate post-level metrics by owner or post type after applying appropriate aggregation (e.g., total views per owner). | Join post-level attributes to user/profile information when enriching posts with owner metadata (one-to-one by OwnerUserId). | Compose into higher-level analyses where post-level rows are the correct grain (e.g., distribution of scores across posts).
params.output_schema: Id: the unique identifier for the post — derived from posts.Id | OwnerUserId: identifier of the user who owns/created the post — derived from posts.OwnerUserId | Score: integer score of the post (votes) — derived from posts.Score | ViewCount: number of times the post has been viewed — derived from posts.ViewCount | CreationDate: timestamp/date when the post was created — derived from posts.CreaionDate (note: source column name in SQL contains a typo 'CreaionDate') | PostTypeId: identifier of the post type (e.g., question, answer) — derived from posts.PostTypeId
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.Score | posts.ViewCount | posts.CreaionDate | posts.PostTypeId
params.metric: Score = posts.Score (base column; not an aggregate in this view) | ViewCount = posts.ViewCount (base column; not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile (or other user-level views) on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = users_basic_profile.Id — safe because users_basic_profile is one-row-per-user and posts_by_owner is one-row-per-post; enriching posts with user attributes does not duplicate post-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a post_type or small dimension table on posts_by_owner.PostTypeId = post_type.Id — safe because post_type is one-row-per-type and will not duplicate post rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example: comments, post_tags, revisions) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply posts_by_owner rows and therefore duplicate per-post measures like ViewCount and Score. Instead, pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., comments_count_by_post with one row per post) and then join on Id to preserve correctness. | when aggregating results from this view (e.g., total views per owner), use an aggregation over posts_by_owner (SUM(ViewCount) GROUP BY OwnerUserId). Do not SUM over a join to a many-side table without grouping/aggregation on that many-side first. | if you need distinct post counts after joining to many-side relations, compute COUNT(DISTINCT posts_by_owner.Id) or perform the aggregation on posts_by_owner first to avoid double-counting.

views.description: Answers who owns each post and basic per-post attributes (score, view count, creation date, post type) at the post Id grain.

views.name: user_badges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM badges

params.description: Lists badge records awarded to users (one row per badge) including badge id, owner, name, and award date.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve all badges or filter badges by user, name, or date. | Report counts of badges per user when aggregated correctly. | Compose badge-level detail with user profile information (one-to-one per user) or with aggregated post/badge metrics. | Filter or join badge-level rows into larger analyses that treat each badge as an atomic event/row.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier for the badge row — derived directly from badges.Id | UserId: identifier of the user who received the badge — derived directly from badges.UserId | Name: name/type of the badge awarded — derived directly from badges.Name | Date: date (or datetime) when the badge was awarded — derived directly from badges.Date
params.grounded_columns: badges.Id | badges.UserId | badges.Name | badges.Date
params.metric: count_badges = COUNT(Id)  -- cardinality-neutral aggregate defined over the view's rows (COUNT of Id returns number of badges) | count_badges_per_user = COUNT(Id) GROUP BY UserId  -- badges per user when grouped by UserId | distinct_badge_names = COUNT(DISTINCT Name)  -- number of distinct badge types in a given filter scope
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile on users_basic_profile.Id = user_badges.UserId — safe because users_basic_profile is one-row-per-user (a 1-to-1 or many-badges-to-one-user relationship). Joining does NOT duplicate badge rows; badges remain the grain (one row per badge). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: do NOT join directly to posts_by_owner on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = user_badges.UserId if you expect badge-level measures (like COUNT(Id)) to remain unchanged, because posts_by_owner is one-to-many (many posts per user) and will multiply badge rows. If you need combined badge+post aggregates, first aggregate the child (e.g., posts_by_owner aggregated to posts_per_user) or aggregate badges after the join to remove duplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: when joining to any other one-to-many table/view on UserId, either (a) join to a pre-aggregated per-user summary of that table, or (b) perform aggregation after the join using DISTINCT or GROUP BY user_badges.Id (or GROUP BY badge Id/UserId) to avoid multiplying badge counts. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: safe to left-join optional 1-to-1 dimension tables keyed by UserId or badge Id (if such a view exists) because they will not duplicate measures; unsafe to join to tables keyed at a lower grain (e.g., posts, comments) without re-aggregation.

views.name: users_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  COALESCE(u.Reputation, 0) AS Reputation,
  u.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users u

params.description: Basic, canonical user core attributes (one row per user): id, display name, creation date, reputation, and linked account id.
params.when_to_use: Look up a user's profile attributes by Id (e.g., display name, creation date, reputation). | Filter or join other datasets to user identity when you need one-row-per-user context. | Compose higher-level metrics per user by aggregating activity (posts, badges) on top of this view. | Return a user list with core profile fields for reporting or downstream enrichment.
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier (derived from table 'users.Id'). | DisplayName: the user's display name as stored (derived from table 'users.DisplayName'). | CreationDate: timestamp when the user account was created (derived from table 'users.CreationDate'). | Reputation: the user's reputation; COALESCE(users.Reputation, 0) — zero if null (derived from table 'users.Reputation' with COALESCE applied). | AccountId: external/account id associated with the user, if any (derived from table 'users.AccountId').
params.grounded_columns: users.Id | users.DisplayName | users.CreationDate | users.Reputation | users.AccountId
params.metric: Reputation = COALESCE(users.Reputation, 0)  -- normalized scalar value per user; not an aggregate
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-row-per-user views/tables on users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-Id so its columns/measures will not be duplicated. Example: JOIN users_basic_profile ON users_core.Id = users_basic_profile.Id | cardinality-UNSAFE caution: do NOT directly join users_core to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., posts_by_owner, user_badges) without aggregation on the many side first, because those joins will multiply users_core rows and therefore duplicate per-user measures like Reputation. Instead, aggregate the many-side first (e.g., posts_by_owner aggregated by OwnerId to counts/sums) and then join the aggregated result to users_core.Id. | safe composition pattern: SELECT u.*, p.post_count FROM users_core u LEFT JOIN (SELECT OwnerId, COUNT(*) AS post_count FROM posts_by_owner GROUP BY OwnerId) p ON u.Id = p.OwnerId | unsafe composition pattern (do not do if you expect Reputation to remain one-per-user): SELECT * FROM users_core u JOIN posts_by_owner p ON u.Id = p.OwnerId — this will produce one row per post and duplicate u.Reputation across those rows, so any SUM/AVG on Reputation would be incorrect unless you re-aggregate appropriately. | Similarly, when joining to user_badges (one-to-many), pre-aggregate badges by UserId when you want badge counts or other badge-level metrics per user, then join to users_core on Id to preserve one-row-per-user semantics.

views.description: Basic, canonical user core attributes (one row per user): id, display name, creation date, reputation, and linked account id.

views.name: user_badges_by_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ub.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(ub.Id) AS badge_count,
  MAX(ub.Date) AS latest_badge_date,
  MAX(ub.Id) AS badge_id -- carry a badge PK to keep joinability
FROM user_badges ub
GROUP BY ub.UserId

params.description: Per-user aggregates of badge activity: count of badges, most recent badge date, plus a representative badge id for joinability.
params.when_to_use: Get badge summary for a specific user (badge count and latest badge date). | Rank or filter users by how many badges they have or by their latest badge date. | Join badge summary to user-level profiles to build enriched user-level datasets (e.g., combine with user metadata or activity aggregates). | Use as a pre-aggregated building block when composing higher-level user analytics without re-scanning the user_badges table.
params.output_schema: UserId: identifier for the user (derived from user_badges.UserId). This is the grouping key / grain of the view. | badge_count: total number of badge records for this user (derived from COUNT(user_badges.Id)). | latest_badge_date: the most recent badge Date for this user (derived from MAX(user_badges.Date)). | badge_id: the maximal badge primary key Id for this user (derived from MAX(user_badges.Id)). This is carried as a representative badge PK to support joinability; it is not guaranteed to correspond to the latest badge unless Id ordering implies recency.
params.grounded_columns: user_badges.Id | user_badges.UserId | user_badges.Date
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(user_badges.Id)  -- one integer per UserId | latest_badge_date = MAX(user_badges.Date)  -- latest Date per UserId | badge_id = MAX(user_badges.Id)  -- representative badge primary key per UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile on UserId — safe because this view is one-row-per-UserId, so joining to a one-row-per-UserId dimension (users_basic_profile or users_core) will not duplicate badge_count or other measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on UserId — safe for the same reason as above. | unsafe-to-join-without-reaggregation: do NOT directly join this view to posts_by_owner (posts_by_owner is one-to-many by UserId) without re-aggregating posts or this view first, because posts_by_owner has multiple rows per UserId and would multiply badge_count and other user-level measures. To combine badge summaries with post-level data, either (a) aggregate posts to the user grain first and then join user-to-user, or (b) join and then re-aggregate at UserId, explicitly controlling for duplication. | unsafe-to-join-without-reaggregation: do NOT join back to the raw user_badges table on UserId expecting badge_count to remain intact, since raw user_badges is one-to-many and will multiply badge_count; instead join to user_badges only when you are selecting badge-level detail (drop or recompute aggregates) or aggregate user_badges separately. | note on badge_id: badge_id is provided only as a join key / representative PK. If you need the latest badge's full row, join user_badges on (user_badges.UserId = UserId AND user_badges.Id = badge_id) only if MAX(Id) corresponds to the desired representative badge; otherwise prefer joining on (user_badges.UserId = UserId AND user_badges.Date = latest_badge_date) and handle ties deterministically.

views.description: Per-user aggregates of badge activity: count of badges, most recent badge date, plus a representative badge id for joinability.

views.name: user_post_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS post_count,
  MAX(p.CreationDate) AS latest_post_date
FROM posts_by_owner p
GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId

params.description: Per-user counts and most-recent post date: how many posts each user (OwnerUserId) has and when their latest post occurred.
params.when_to_use: Get total number of posts for a given user or set of users (e.g., leaderboard, user summaries). | Enrich user profile rows with post_count and latest_post_date without recalculating from posts. | Compose into higher-level metrics that need per-user post aggregates (e.g., posts per active user, retention snapshots) while preserving per-user grain. | Filter users by activity (e.g., users with post_count > N or latest_post_date within a range) before joining to other datasets.
params.output_schema: OwnerUserId: the user identifier at the view grain; sourced from posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId (GROUP BY key). | post_count: integer count of posts for this OwnerUserId; derived from COUNT(posts_by_owner.Id). | latest_post_date: timestamp of the most recent post for this OwnerUserId; derived from MAX(posts_by_owner.CreationDate).
params.grounded_columns: posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId | posts_by_owner.Id | posts_by_owner.CreationDate
params.metric: post_count = COUNT(posts_by_owner.Id) -- per OwnerUserId aggregate (one row per OwnerUserId) | latest_post_date = MAX(posts_by_owner.CreationDate) -- per OwnerUserId aggregate
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile (NORM) on OwnerUserId = users_basic_profile.Id — safe because users_basic_profile is one row per user so this view remains one-row-per-user and measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (NORM) on OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe for same reason (one row per user). | cardinality-UNSAFE: do NOT directly join to posts_by_owner (SEL) on OwnerUserId without re-aggregating the posts side (or aggregating the joined result back to OwnerUserId), because posts_by_owner is one-to-many (multiple posts per user) and will multiply post_count and distort latest_post_date. | cardinality-UNSAFE: do NOT directly join to user_badges (SEL) or user_badges_by_user (AGG) on OwnerUserId if the badge side is one-to-many (multiple badge rows per user) unless you first: (a) aggregate the badge side to one row per OwnerUserId, or (b) re-aggregate the joined result back to OwnerUserId. Joining without re-aggregation would duplicate this view's measures. | safe composition pattern for enrichment: LEFT JOIN users_basic_profile ON user_post_counts.OwnerUserId = users_basic_profile.Id — preserves one row per OwnerUserId; use LEFT JOIN if you want users with posts only or INNER JOIN if restricting to users present in both. | safe composition pattern for combining with another per-user aggregate view (e.g., user_badges_by_user): JOIN on OwnerUserId when both sides are aggregated to one row per user — the planner can SUM or otherwise combine metrics knowing the key is one-to-one at the user grain. | when composing into larger queries that change grain (e.g., aggregating to a cohort or day): always re-aggregate post_count (e.g., SUM(post_count) over the desired grouping) rather than assuming additivity across arbitrary joins; latest_post_date should be recomputed as the appropriate aggregate (e.g., MAX(latest_post_date)) after any join that can reduce or expand the user set.

views.description: Per-user counts and most-recent post date: how many posts each user (OwnerUserId) has and when their latest post occurred.

views.name: users_core_6
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  u.Location AS Location
FROM users AS u

params.description: A one-row-per-user core profile view exposing user id, display name, last access, reputation, creation date, and location.
params.when_to_use: Look up basic profile attributes for a specific user or set of users (by Id). | Filter or join users by creation date, last access date, reputation, or location. | Serve as the user-side dimension when composing queries that aggregate facts by user (after ensuring aggregates are computed from one-to-many children). | Enrich post, badge, or activity aggregates with user display name and profile timestamps.
params.output_schema: Id: user identifier — derived from users.Id | DisplayName: user's display name — derived from users.DisplayName | LastAccessDate: timestamp of the user's last access — derived from users.LastAccessDate | Reputation: user's reputation score (stored integer) — derived from users.Reputation | CreationDate: timestamp when the user account was created — derived from users.CreationDate | Location: free-text location string from the user's profile — derived from users.Location
params.grounded_columns: users.Id | users.DisplayName | users.LastAccessDate | users.Reputation | users.CreationDate | users.Location
params.metric: Id = users.Id | DisplayName = users.DisplayName | LastAccessDate = users.LastAccessDate | Reputation = users.Reputation | CreationDate = users.CreationDate | Location = users.Location
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile on Id — safe because both are one-row-per-Id normalized views and will not duplicate rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_post_counts (AGG) on Id — safe because user_post_counts is pre-aggregated to one row per user (Id) so this view's measures are not multiplied; use LEFT JOIN if you want users with zero posts. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badges_by_user (AGG) on Id — safe because that sibling is aggregated per user; it will not duplicate this view's rows. | do NOT directly join users_core_6 to raw one-to-many tables such as posts_by_owner (SEL) or user_badges (SEL) without aggregation, because posts_by_owner and user_badges contain multiple rows per users.Id and would multiply/duplicate users_core_6 rows and any measures derived from it. | If you need badge or post-level detail, either (a) aggregate posts_by_owner or user_badges to one row per users.Id (e.g., COUNT(*), SUM(...)) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate with GROUP BY users.Id to restore one-row-per-user cardinality. | When joining to other user-level views (users_core, users_basic_profile), prefer equality on Id. These joins are safe because all referenced views are normalized NORM views at the same grain (Id). | When composing metrics that sum or average Reputation, use this view as a dimension (group by Id or aggregate users_core_6.Reputation) but avoid joining it to one-to-many child tables without proper aggregation to prevent inflated aggregates.

views.description: A one-row-per-user core profile view exposing user id, display name, last access, reputation, creation date, and location.

views.name: posts_minimal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts p

params.description: Row-level representation of posts with a minimal set of identifying, temporal, and engagement columns (one row per post).
params.when_to_use: Fetch or filter individual posts by id, owner, type, creation date, title, or tags. | Compute post-level metrics (score, view count) or join post rows to user/profile dimensions while preserving one-row-per-post granularity. | Compose aggregations at the post grain (e.g., counts of posts, sums/averages of Score or ViewCount) or build further aggregations grouped by OwnerUserId, PostTypeId, CreationDate buckets, or Tags.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the post — derived from posts.Id | OwnerUserId: user id of the post owner — derived from posts.OwnerUserId | PostTypeId: numeric code for post type (e.g., question/answer) — derived from posts.PostTypeId | CreationDate: creation timestamp of the post — derived from posts.CreaionDate (note: spelled CreaionDate in the underlying SELECT) | Score: post score (votes) — derived from posts.Score | ViewCount: number of views on the post — derived from posts.ViewCount | Title: post title text — derived from posts.Title | Tags: post tags string (usually angle-bracket delimited) — derived from posts.Tags
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.PostTypeId | posts.CreaionDate | posts.Score | posts.ViewCount | posts.Title | posts.Tags
params.metric: Id = posts.Id | OwnerUserId = posts.OwnerUserId | PostTypeId = posts.PostTypeId | CreationDate = posts.CreaionDate | Score = posts.Score | ViewCount = posts.ViewCount | Title = posts.Title | Tags = posts.Tags | post_count = COUNT(posts.Id)  -- derived metric when aggregating this view at a higher level (not present in the view itself) | sum_Score = SUM(Score)  -- valid when aggregating rows of this view | avg_Score = AVG(Score)  -- valid when aggregating rows of this view | sum_ViewCount = SUM(ViewCount)  -- valid when aggregating rows of this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or users_basic_profile, users_core_6) on posts_minimal.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user (this will not duplicate post rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner on posts_minimal.OwnerUserId = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId only when posts_by_owner is an alternate representation of posts at the same post-grain (ensure posts_by_owner is not a one-to-many expansion). If posts_by_owner is one-row-per-owner with aggregated metrics, joining on OwnerUserId is safe and will not duplicate post-level rows but will repeat owner-level aggregates for each post row (which is typically desired when enriching posts). | do NOT join posts_minimal to user_badges or user_badges_by_user directly without re-aggregation: those are one-to-many (multiple badges per user) and joining them on OwnerUserId will multiply post rows and thereby inflate post-level measures (Score, ViewCount) unless you first aggregate badges to one row per user (for example, badges_count = COUNT(*) GROUP BY UserId) and then join that aggregated result to posts_minimal on OwnerUserId. | do NOT join to user_post_counts (if user_post_counts is one-row-per-user aggregated counts) without understanding intended semantics: joining an aggregated-per-user table to posts_minimal will repeat the per-user metric for every post of that user (this is safe if you intend a per-post enrichment, but not if you expect a preserved post-level sum of metrics from the aggregated table). If you need to produce user-level aggregates from posts_minimal, instead aggregate posts_minimal (GROUP BY OwnerUserId) and then join to user-level tables. | when composing to compute higher-level metrics (e.g., per-user totals), prefer: SELECT OwnerUserId, COUNT(*) AS posts_by_user, SUM(Score) AS total_score FROM posts_minimal GROUP BY OwnerUserId; then join that aggregated result to one-row-per-user dimensions safely. | joins that will not duplicate this view's measures: any join to a table/view that is one-row-per-key where key = OwnerUserId or key = Id (for example users_core keyed by Id) — these preserve the one-row-per-post cardinality and do not multiply Score/ViewCount. | joins that multiply rows (and therefore require re-aggregation): joins to badge tables, comments, tags-as-rows tables (if tags are normalized to many rows), or any child entity with many rows per post or per user — such joins will duplicate post rows and must be followed by proper aggregation (e.g., SUM(Score) grouped by post Id) or replaced by pre-aggregated summaries.

views.description: Row-level representation of posts with a minimal set of identifying, temporal, and engagement columns (one row per post).

views.name: posts_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id

params.description: Returns one row per post with post id, title, owner user id, and a resolved owner display name (preferring the post's OwnerDisplayName, falling back to the users table DisplayName).
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic post metadata for a single post or a set of posts (id, title, owner id, owner display name). | Compose queries that need post-level attributes as a starting point for further aggregation (for example, counts of related records per post or joins to per-post metrics). | Present lists of posts with owner information in UIs or reports where a single display name per post is required.
params.output_schema: Id: post identifier, derived from posts.Id | Title: post title, derived from posts.Title | OwnerUserId: identifier of the user who owns the post, derived from posts.OwnerUserId | OwnerDisplayName: resolved display name for the post owner; expression COALESCE(posts.OwnerDisplayName, users.DisplayName) where users.DisplayName comes from users.DisplayName and posts.OwnerDisplayName comes from posts.OwnerDisplayName
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.Title | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.OwnerDisplayName | users.Id | users.DisplayName
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All outputs are row-level/pass-through or simple expression values: | OwnerDisplayName = COALESCE(posts.OwnerDisplayName, users.DisplayName)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or users_basic_profile / users_core_6) on posts_core.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_* are one-row-per-user dimensions (one user row per Id), so joining will not duplicate posts_core rows or change post-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_post_counts (AGG) on posts_core.OwnerUserId = user_post_counts.UserId — safe when you intend to attach per-user aggregates; user_post_counts is one-row-per-user so it will not duplicate post rows. | cardinality-UNSAFE guidance: do NOT directly join posts_core to one-to-many tables/views such as user_badges (SEL) or user_badges_by_user (if that is one-to-many) on OwnerUserId without aggregation, because those are one-to-many from user -> badges and would multiply post rows (duplicating the post-level attributes). Instead, aggregate badges to one row per user (for example via user_badges_by_user or an aggregate subquery that produces one row per user) and then join on OwnerUserId. | cardinality-UNSAFE guidance: do NOT join posts_core to posts_by_owner (SEL) on OwnerUserId expecting to preserve one row per post — posts_by_owner represents multiple posts per owner and would duplicate or incorrectly expand rows. If combining post-level details with owner-level lists, either (a) join to an owner-level aggregate or (b) use posts_by_owner in a separate query context (e.g., to derive per-owner lists) and then link via OwnerUserId after appropriate aggregation. | When composing additional aggregates on top of posts_core (for example, counts of comments per post), perform aggregation grouped by posts_core.Id to avoid accidental duplication from joining to many-sided tables. | Planner notes: posts_core is normalized (one row per posts.Id). Any join on posts_core.Id is one-to-one (or one-to-zero) if the other side is a unique-per-post relation (for example, a post-metadata table keyed by Id). Any join on OwnerUserId must respect the cardinality of the right-hand side: safe for one-row-per-user dimensions/AGG, unsafe for user->many relationships without pre-aggregation.

params.output_schema: comments.Id: Primary identifier of the comment row — derived from base table column comments.Id | comments.UserId: Id of the user who authored the comment — derived from base table column comments.UserId | comments.CreationDate: Timestamp when the comment was created — derived from base table column comments.CreationDate | comments.PostId: Foreign key referencing the parent post — derived from base table column comments.PostId | posts.FavoriteCount: Numeric favorite count of the joined post — derived from base table column posts.FavoriteCount | posts.Id AS post_Id: The joined post's Id (same as posts.Id) — derived from base table column posts.Id

Example safe derived metrics to compute on top of this view: | comment_count = COUNT(comments.Id)  -- count of comments in the selected scope | distinct_user_count = COUNT(DISTINCT comments.UserId)  -- distinct commenters | comments_per_post = COUNT(comments.Id) GROUP BY comments.PostId  -- must group by comments.PostId to get per-post counts

Examples: | Join to users_core (or users_basic_profile, users_core_6) on comments.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because each comment has exactly one user and the user tables are one-row-per-user, so comment-level rows remain one-to-one to user rows. | Join to posts_core or posts_minimal on comments.PostId = posts.Id — safe for enrichment because posts are one-row-per-post; duplications will not occur because the view already has at most one matching post row due to the LEFT JOIN in the view. | Join to posts_with_owner or posts_with_owner_name on comments.PostId = posts_with_owner.Id — safe for the same reason as posts_core (one-row-per-post). |  | cardinality-UNSAFE (do NOT join directly without re-aggregation) guidance: do NOT directly join this view to any table or view that is one-to-many from posts or comments (i.e., that can have multiple rows per comments.Id or per posts.Id) unless you re-aggregate first, because it will multiply comment-level rows and any measures computed from them. views.name: users_with_post_counts

  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  COALESCE(p.post_count, 0) AS post_count
FROM users AS u

FROM votes

params.description: One-row-per-vote detailed view: returns each vote record with its core attributes (which post, vote type, when, who, bounty amount).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve or filter individual votes (e.g., find all votes on a post, votes by a user, or votes in a date range). | Build aggregations over votes (counts, sums of bounty amounts, time-based trends) by composing/grouping on PostId, UserId, VoteTypeId, CreationDate, or Id. | Join vote-level details to other entities (posts, users) when you need vote-level granularity before aggregation.

params.metric: vote_count = COUNT(Id)  -- a row-count aggregation over Id yields number of votes | distinct_voters = COUNT(DISTINCT UserId)  -- number of unique users in a group | bounty_sum = SUM(BountyAmount)  -- total bounty amount in a group (NULLs should be treated per SQL semantics) | per_vote_flag = ANY_NON_NULL(Id)  -- identity measure: each row represents one vote (use COUNT(Id) rather than SUM on a measure to avoid duplication issues)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_core (or posts_minimal, posts_with_owner, posts_with_owner_name, posts_row_level, posts_by_owner) on votes_row_level.PostId = posts_core.Id — safe when you keep results at vote-grain because posts are one row per post; joining adds post attributes without duplicating vote rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or users_basic_profile, users_core_6) on votes_row_level.UserId = users_core.Id — safe when you keep vote-grain results because users are one row per user; adds user attributes without duplicating votes. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children of votes (there are typically no children keyed to votes.Id in the provided sibling list) or to any aggregation that is many-per-vote without re-aggregation — doing so would multiply vote-level rows and thus duplicate counts/sums. Instead, aggregate the one-to-many side first (e.g., GROUP BY votes_row_level.Id and produce single-row-per-vote metrics) then join, or join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain. | do NOT join to user_badges or user_badges_by_user on UserId without re-aggregation if you plan to preserve vote-level measures: user_badges_by_user is an agg per user and can be safely joined on UserId if it's one-row-per-user; but raw user_badges (SEL) is many badges per user and will duplicate vote rows for users with multiple badges — if you need badge counts per vote's user, pre-aggregate badges to one row per user (e.g., badge_count = COUNT(*) GROUP BY UserId) then join on UserId. | when composing higher-level metrics (e.g., votes per post, bounty sum per post), prefer aggregating votes_row_level directly: GROUP BY PostId to compute vote_count_per_post = COUNT(Id) and bounty_sum_per_post = SUM(BountyAmount). This avoids joining at vote-grain to post-side one-to-many tables which would otherwise require DISTINCT or re-aggregation to maintain correct measures. | example safe composition patterns: | - To get votes per post: SELECT PostId, COUNT(Id) AS vote_count, SUM(BountyAmount) AS bounty_sum FROM votes_row_level GROUP BY PostId; then join results to posts_minimal on PostId = posts_minimal.Id (safe because aggregation produced one-row-per-post). | - To get votes by user with user profile: aggregate or keep at vote-grain and join users_core on UserId = users_core.Id (safe because users_core is one-row-per-user). | - To enrich with badge counts per voter: pre-aggregate user_badges (or use user_badges_by_user if available and one-row-per-user) to badge_count_by_user, then join on UserId — safe because the badge side is one-row-per-user.

params.when_to_use: List or search comments for a given post or user (e.g., show all comments for post X). | Join comment metadata to post or user information (e.g., display comment author name alongside comment). | Filter comments by creation date ranges or by author for analytics or UI displays. | Compose aggregates at the post or user level by grouping this view (e.g., count comments per post).

Instead, pre-aggregate badges (e.g., badge_count BY UserId) and join the aggregated result on UserId. | do NOT join comments_by_post to posts_by_owner or posts_with_owner (one-to-many from owner to posts) in a way that matches multiple post rows per PostId; if you need post-level aggregates (e.g., total posts by the comment's post owner) aggregate posts_by_owner first to one row per owner, then join on owner Id to avoid multiplying comment rows. | When composing metrics at a higher grain (e.g., comments per post or comments per user), perform explicit aggregation on comments_by_post (GROUP BY PostId or UserId) rather than relying on implicit multiplicative joins. | When joining to any sibling AGG view (e.g., user_post_counts, user_badges_by_user), ensure those AGG views are one-row-per-key and join on the key (UserId or PostId) — these are safe because they have been aggregated to the corresponding key and will not multiply comment rows.

views.name: badges_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  badges.Date AS Date
FROM badges
WHERE badges.UserId IS NOT NULL

params.description: Row-level view of badges awarded to users (one row per badge) for questions about individual badge records and for composing badge-level counts by user.
params.when_to_use: List badges (Id, UserId, Name, Date) for display or filtering | Filter badges by user, date, or name and then aggregate (e.g., count badges by user or name) | Join badge rows to user information when you need badge-level detail along with user attributes | Compose into aggregated summaries (e.g., badges per user) by grouping on UserId

params.grounded_columns: badges.Id | badges.UserId | badges.Name | badges.Date

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core or users_basic_profile on badges_row_level.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because badges_row_level is one row per badge; joining to the user dimension (one user row per Id) will not duplicate badge-level rows and preserves badge counts. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core_6 or users_basic_profile (any one-row-per-user normalized user view) on UserId = Id — safe for attaching user attributes to each badge row. | do NOT join directly to posts_by_owner, posts_row_level, posts_core, posts_minimal, posts_with_owner_name, or any posts_* view that is one-to-many from user without re-aggregation — joining badges_row_level to a user->many-posts table on UserId = OwnerUserId will multiply badge rows per post and will inflate badge-level aggregates unless you first aggregate posts to one row per user (for example, join to user_post_counts which is pre-aggregated by user). | safe composition pattern for aggregations: to compute badges per user, GROUP BY badges_row_level.UserId and use count_badges; if you need post-related metrics combined with badge counts, join badges_row_level aggregated to user_post_counts or user_badges_by_user (both are pre-aggregated) on UserId to avoid row multiplication. | When joining to other badge-level or row-level views (e.g., user_badges which may have similar grain), ensure keys align (Id or UserId) and be aware of potential duplicates if the other view has the same badge row duplicated; prefer joining on Id for one-to-one badge merges.

views.name: badges_per_user_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(b.Id) AS badge_count,
  MIN(b.Date) AS first_badge_date,
  MAX(b.Date) AS last_badge_date
FROM badges b
WHERE b.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY b.UserId

params.description: Per-user aggregated badge metrics: count of badges and first/last badge dates per user.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of badges earned by each user (badge counts) and the range of badge dates per user | Filter or segment users by having earned at least one badge, or by first/last badge date windows | Compose with user-level dimensions (profiles, cores) to show badge metrics alongside user attributes | As a safe aggregated input when joining to other one-row-per-user datasets (e.g., user profiles) to enrich user-level reports
params.output_schema: UserId: the user's identifier (sourced from badges.UserId) | badge_count: integer count of badge rows for the user (derived from COUNT(badges.Id)) | first_badge_date: earliest badge date for the user (derived from MIN(badges.Date)) | last_badge_date: latest badge date for the user (derived from MAX(badges.Date))
params.grounded_columns: badges.UserId | badges.Id | badges.Date
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(badges.Id)  -- count of badge rows per UserId | first_badge_date = MIN(badges.Date)  -- earliest badges.Date per UserId | last_badge_date = MAX(badges.Date)  -- latest badges.Date per UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile, users_core, users_core_6 or any other one-row-per-user view/table on UserId — safe because badges_per_user_agg has exactly one row per UserId (the grouped grain), so joining on UserId will not duplicate badge_count or the date measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_post_counts or user_badges_by_user (both are also user-level aggregates) on UserId — safe to join directly since both sides are one-row-per-user aggregates; if combining numeric measures, be explicit about aggregation (e.g., SUM or AVG across users) in the consuming query. | Do NOT join directly to posts_by_owner, posts_core, posts_minimal, posts_with_owner, posts_with_owner_name, posts_row_level or any other one-to-many post-level table on UserId without re-aggregating the post-level table first — such joins will multiply this view's per-user badge_count and date metrics because those tables contain multiple rows per UserId. | Do NOT join directly to user_badges (a badge-level selection) on UserId without re-aggregating user_badges first — joining a many-row-per-user set will duplicate badge_count and distort MIN/MAX unless you re-aggregate or join on keys that preserve one-row-per-user (for example, join badge-level data with an aggregation that collapses to UserId before combining). | If you need badge metrics combined with another one-to-many measure (e.g., post counts by post type), either: (a) aggregate the other table to one-row-per-UserId first and then join on UserId, or (b) join at detail level and re-aggregate both measures in the consuming query, making sure to use appropriate aggregations and GROUP BY UserId. | When composing with sibling aggregated views, be explicit about which aggregates you intend to combine (e.g., sum of badge_count across a segment of users) — the planner can treat this view as a stable one-row-per-user source.

views.description: Per-user aggregated badge metrics: count of badges and first/last badge dates per user.

views.name: users_badge_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  COALESCE(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count,
  b.first_badge_date AS first_badge_date,
  b.last_badge_date AS last_badge_date
FROM users_basic_profile u
LEFT JOIN badges_per_user_agg b
  ON b.UserId = u.Id
WHERE u.Id IS NOT NULL

params.description: Denormalized per-user summary combining basic user profile with aggregated badge metrics (counts and first/last badge dates).
params.when_to_use: Get a one-row-per-user profile that includes badge statistics (total badges, date of first and last badge). | Compose user-level analyses that need both profile attributes (DisplayName, Reputation) and badge aggregates without re-joining raw badge rows. | Filter or rank users by badge_count, first_badge_date, last_badge_date, or combine those with reputation/DisplayName.
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier — derived from users_basic_profile.Id | DisplayName: the user's display name — derived from users_basic_profile.DisplayName | Reputation: the user's reputation score — derived from users_basic_profile.Reputation | badge_count: total number of badges for the user (0 when no badges) — derived from badges_per_user_agg.badge_count with COALESCE to 0 | first_badge_date: date/time of the user's earliest badge — derived from badges_per_user_agg.first_badge_date | last_badge_date: date/time of the user's most recent badge — derived from badges_per_user_agg.last_badge_date
params.grounded_columns: users_basic_profile.Id | users_basic_profile.DisplayName | users_basic_profile.Reputation | badges_per_user_agg.UserId | badges_per_user_agg.badge_count | badges_per_user_agg.first_badge_date | badges_per_user_agg.last_badge_date
params.metric: badge_count = COALESCE(badges_per_user_agg.badge_count, 0)  -- badge_count is taken directly from the pre-aggregated badges_per_user_agg table; COALESCE ensures users with no row in badges_per_user_agg show 0 | first_badge_date = badges_per_user_agg.first_badge_date  -- earliest badge date as provided by badges_per_user_agg (NULL when no badges) | last_badge_date = badges_per_user_agg.last_badge_date  -- latest badge date as provided by badges_per_user_agg (NULL when no badges)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-user (for example users_basic_profile itself or other one-row-per-user normalized views such as users_core, users_core_6) on Id = <their user id column> — safe because users_badge_denorm is one-row-per-user (grain = Id) so measures like badge_count will not be duplicated. | You can join safely to user-level aggregated views (e.g., user_post_counts, user_badges_by_user) on Id = <their UserId/Id> only if those views are also one-row-per-user (i.e., aggregated at UserId). Since both sides are at the same grain, measures remain correct. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or row-level views (for example posts_by_owner, posts_row_level, user_badges, posts_core, posts_with_owner, posts_with_owner_name) without first aggregating the many-side up to one row per user. Joining to a raw/many-side table will multiply rows and therefore duplicate badge_count and any other user-level measures. If you need to combine with posts, first aggregate posts (e.g., COUNT(*) AS post_count GROUP BY OwnerUserId) and then join that aggregation to this view on Id = OwnerUserId. | If you need to compute derived user-level metrics that combine badge_count with another many-side metric (e.g., badges per post), ensure both inputs are aggregated to user-level first, then join on Id to avoid incorrect multiplication. | If you must join to a many-to-many intermediate (rare for user joins), re-aggregate after the join back to user-level to guarantee correctness.

views.description: Denormalized per-user summary combining basic user profile with aggregated badge metrics (counts and first/last badge dates).

views.name: posts_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId
FROM posts

params.description: Base normalized view of posts at the post (Id) grain: returns core post attributes such as owner, view count, title, type, and parent linkage.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve or filter individual posts and their basic attributes | Compose higher-level aggregations by grouping posts (e.g., counts, sums of ViewCount) while preserving one-row-per-post semantics | Join post-level attributes to user or parent-post dimensions without duplicating post-level measures | Serve as the canonical input when computing metrics per post (e.g., total views per post, posts per owner after aggregation)
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier for the post — derived from posts.Id | OwnerUserId: identifier of the user who owns/created the post — derived from posts.OwnerUserId | ViewCount: number of times the post has been viewed — derived from posts.ViewCount | Title: post title text — derived from posts.Title | PostTypeId: numeric code indicating the post type (e.g., question/answer) — derived from posts.PostTypeId | ParentId: for answers, the Id of the parent question; NULL for top-level posts — derived from posts.ParentId
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.ViewCount | posts.Title | posts.PostTypeId | posts.ParentId
params.metric: ViewCount = posts.ViewCount (base numeric column; not an aggregate in this view) | Post_count = COUNT(posts.Id) when aggregated by downstream query (this view is at post grain so counts must be computed by aggregating Id) | Views_sum = SUM(posts.ViewCount) when aggregated by downstream query (must aggregate ViewCount explicitly)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core or users_basic_profile on posts.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core (user) is one-row-per-user, joining a one-row-per-post stream to a one-row-per-user dimension does NOT duplicate post rows or their measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts (self) derived single-row-per-post views such as posts_minimal or posts_core on Id — safe because those are one-row-per-post so joins preserve row-level uniqueness. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a parent-post dimension (another one-row-per-post view) on posts.ParentId = parent.Id — safe for enriching answer rows with parent question attributes when ParentId is non-null; still one-row-per-post. | do NOT join without aggregation to user_badges, user_badges_by_user, posts_by_owner, user_post_counts, or other one-to-many tables/views producing multiple rows per OwnerUserId (badge rows, per-user multiple posts aggregated differently) because those are one-to-many relative to users or posts and will multiply posts' rows and thereby duplicate ViewCount and other post-level measures. | If you need badge information or other one-to-many detail per post/owner, first aggregate that one-to-many source to one row per join key (e.g., user: COUNT(badges) AS badge_count by OwnerUserId) and then join on OwnerUserId — this preserves cardinality and prevents measure duplication. | When joining to aggregated views like user_post_counts (already per-user aggregates), verify their grain (one-row-per-user) and join on OwnerUserId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-key or post-to-user is many-to-one. | When composing further aggregations that combine posts with other dimensions, always re-aggregate post-level measures (e.g., SUM(ViewCount)) after joins that increase cardinality or after bringing in many-to-many relationships.

views.description: Base normalized view of posts at the post (Id) grain: returns core post attributes such as owner, view count, title, type, and parent linkage.

views.name: posthistory_by_user_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId AS PostId,
  UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS history_count,
  MIN(CreationDate) AS first_history_date,
  MAX(CreationDate) AS last_history_date
FROM postHistory
GROUP BY UserId, PostId

params.description: Per-user-per-post aggregated history: counts and first/last history timestamps for each (UserId, PostId) pair from postHistory.
params.when_to_use: How many postHistory events a given user generated on a specific post (history_count). | When a user first/last modified or had history entries for a specific post (first_history_date, last_history_date). | Filtering or summarizing postHistory by user and post before joining to user or post dimensions (as a pre-aggregated building block). | Composing higher-level metrics like total distinct post interactions per user (by summing history_count or counting rows) when joined safely and/or re-aggregated.
params.output_schema: UserId: the user identifier associated with the history rows — derived from postHistory.UserId | PostId: the post identifier associated with the history rows — derived from postHistory.PostId | history_count: number of postHistory rows for this (UserId, PostId) pair — derived from COUNT(*) over grouped postHistory rows | first_history_date: earliest CreationDate for this (UserId, PostId) pair — derived from MIN(postHistory.CreationDate) | last_history_date: latest CreationDate for this (UserId, PostId) pair — derived from MAX(postHistory.CreationDate)
params.grounded_columns: postHistory.PostId | postHistory.UserId | postHistory.CreationDate
params.metric: history_count = COUNT(*) grouped by (postHistory.UserId, postHistory.PostId) | first_history_date = MIN(postHistory.CreationDate) grouped by (postHistory.UserId, postHistory.PostId) | last_history_date = MAX(postHistory.CreationDate) grouped by (postHistory.UserId, postHistory.PostId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_basic_profile, users_core, users_core_6 (or any user dimension that is one-row-per-UserId) on UserId — safe because those are user-level dimensions (one row per UserId) so this view's rows remain one-per-(UserId,PostId) and its aggregated measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_minimal, posts_core, posts_row_level, posts_by_owner, posts_with_owner_name, posts_with_owner (or any post dimension that is one-row-per-PostId) on PostId — safe because those are post-level dimensions (one row per PostId) so this view's rows remain one-per-(UserId,PostId) and its aggregated measures are not duplicated. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many siblings such as user_badges, user_badges_by_user, or other aggregate/detail tables that can have multiple rows per the same UserId without re-aggregation, because joining them will multiply rows for the same (UserId,PostId) and therefore overcount history_count. If you must combine with a one-to-many table, first aggregate that table to one row per join key (for example, one row per UserId or per PostId) or re-aggregate the combined result back to the desired grain. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (for example, total history events per UserId), aggregate this view's history_count by summing history_count grouped by UserId. That is safe because history_count is already at the (UserId,PostId) grain; summing over PostId yields correct totals. | If joining to another table on UserId and PostId simultaneously, ensure the other side is at most one row per (UserId,PostId). If the other side is at a coarser grain (only UserId or only PostId), join on that key and then re-aggregate to avoid duplication (e.g., to compute per-user totals from a joined per-post table, group by UserId and sum history_count). | Avoid joining to raw postHistory again without grouping, because that would recreate a many-to-many relationship and duplicate the aggregated measures.

views.description: Per-user-per-post aggregated history: counts and first/last history timestamps for each (UserId, PostId) pair from postHistory.

views.name: users_with_posts_and_history_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.ViewCount IS NOT NULL AND p.ViewCount > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS owned_high_view_post_count,
  COALESCE(ph_distinct.posthistory_distinct_post_count, 0) AS posthistory_distinct_post_count,
  COALESCE(ph_multi.posts_with_multiple_rows_count, 0) AS posthistory_posts_with_multiple_rows_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN posts p
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
-- Note: threshold for "high view" is left as a question_op; here we count posts with non-null ViewCount > 0.
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    UserId,
    COUNT(DISTINCT PostId) AS posthistory_distinct_post_count
  FROM postHistory
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) ph_distinct
  ON ph_distinct.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    UserId,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE history_count > 1) AS posts_with_multiple_rows_count
  FROM (
    SELECT UserId, PostId, COUNT(*) AS history_count
    FROM postHistory
    WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY UserId, PostId
  ) up
  GROUP BY UserId
) ph_multi
  ON ph_multi.UserId = u.Id
GROUP BY u.Id, u.DisplayName, ph_distinct.posthistory_distinct_post_count, ph_multi.posts_with_multiple_rows_count

params.description: Per-user aggregated counts combining user profile with counts of their owned posts meeting a view threshold and two postHistory-derived metrics (distinct posts touched and posts with multiple history rows).
params.when_to_use: Get per-user counts of owned posts with positive view counts alongside postHistory summary metrics for reporting or leaderboards. | Compose dashboards showing users with both activity on posts (high-view posts) and history activity (distinct posts touched, posts with multiple history entries). | Join with other user-level dimensions to enrich user profiles when you need counts pre-aggregated at the user grain.
params.output_schema: Id: user's unique identifier, from users.Id | DisplayName: user's display name, from users.DisplayName | owned_high_view_post_count: integer count of this user's owned posts that have a non-null ViewCount > 0; derived from posts.ViewCount with aggregation SUM(CASE WHEN p.ViewCount IS NOT NULL AND p.ViewCount > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) grouped by users.Id | posthistory_distinct_post_count: integer count of distinct PostId values in postHistory for this user (ignores NULL UserId); derived from COUNT(DISTINCT postHistory.PostId) in the ph_distinct subquery (ph_distinct.posthistory_distinct_post_count) | posthistory_posts_with_multiple_rows_count: integer count of PostId values for this user that have more than one row in postHistory (i.e., posts with history_count > 1); derived from COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE history_count > 1) over the per-(UserId,PostId) counts computed from postHistory in ph_multi (ph_multi.posts_with_multiple_rows_count)
params.grounded_columns: users.Id | users.DisplayName | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.ViewCount | postHistory.UserId | postHistory.PostId
params.metric: owned_high_view_post_count = SUM(CASE WHEN posts.ViewCount IS NOT NULL AND posts.ViewCount > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY users.Id | posthistory_distinct_post_count = COUNT(DISTINCT postHistory.PostId) FILTER (WHERE postHistory.UserId IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY postHistory.UserId (joined to users.Id) | posthistory_posts_with_multiple_rows_count = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE history_count > 1) where history_count = COUNT(*) GROUP BY postHistory.UserId, postHistory.PostId (computed in subquery) then aggregated to UserId and joined to users.Id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other user-level (one-row-per-user) dimension or normalized user views on users.Id (e.g., users_core, users_basic_profile, users_core_6) — safe because this view is one row per users.Id (its GROUP BY is users.Id, DisplayName and the ph_* columns are at user granularity) so counts will not be duplicated. | You can safely join this view to SELECT or NORM user-level views on users.Id without re-aggregation (preserves measures). | Do NOT directly inner-join or left-join this view to multi-row tables keyed by users.Id (for example: posts, postHistory, user_badges_by_user, user_post_counts if those are at a lower-than-user grain with multiple rows per user) unless you first aggregate that other source to one row per users.Id or you re-aggregate after the join. Joining to one-to-many tables will multiply owned_high_view_post_count and the postHistory-derived counts. | If you need to combine with post-level views (e.g., posts_by_owner, posts_core, posts_with_owner), aggregate those post-level rows up to users.Id (for example SUM, COUNT, MAX as appropriate) before joining, or join in a subquery and re-aggregate at users.Id to avoid duplicating this view's measures. | If you need to compute ratios or derived metrics that combine this view's counts with other measures coming from many-row children, compute the child aggregates at user granularity first and then join on users.Id to keep cardinality stable.

views.description: Per-user aggregated counts combining user profile with counts of their owned posts meeting a view threshold and two postHistory-derived metrics (distinct posts touched and posts with multiple history rows).

views.name: badges_row_level_58

  badges.Date AS Date,

params.description: Row-level view of badges: one row per badge with user, name, date, and derived award year.

params.grounded_columns: badges.Id | badges.UserId | badges.Name | badges.Date
params.metric: award_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER)  -- derived scalar expression producing the award calendar year from badges.Date
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core or users_basic_profile on badges.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because both users tables are one-row-per-user, so joining user attributes does not duplicate badge rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core_6 on badges.UserId = users_core_6.Id — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-user). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner_name or posts_core on badges.UserId = posts_core.OwnerUserId only when you first aggregate posts to one row per OwnerUserId (for example, compute post counts or other aggregates). params.description: A normalized row-level view of vote events with the vote year parsed from CreationDate (one row per votes.Id).

If joining to an AGG view that is one-row-per-user (e.g., user_post_counts if it is one-row-per-user), it is safe. views.name: posts_with_owner_68
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.AnswerCount AS "posts.AnswerCount",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.Tags AS "posts.Tags",
  users.Id AS "users.Id AS Owner_Id",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName AS Owner_DisplayName"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId

params.description: Provides posts (by post Id) with selected post fields and the owning user's id and display name — useful for reporting post metadata alongside owner identity.
params.when_to_use: Lookup post metadata together with the owner's basic identity (id and display name) for a given post or set of posts. | Compose higher-level queries that need one row per post plus owner attributes (e.g., filter posts by owner display name, select posts with their owner for presentation). | Join this post-level view to other one-row-per-post aggregates without duplicating post-level measures.
params.output_schema: posts.Id: the primary key of the post — derived from posts.Id in the base posts table (this view is at the grain posts.Id). | posts.OwnerUserId: foreign key referencing the post owner — derived from posts.OwnerUserId in posts. | posts.AnswerCount: number of answers recorded on the post row — derived from posts.AnswerCount in posts (no aggregation in this view). | posts.Title: post title text — derived from posts.Title in posts. | posts.Tags: tags string for the post (as stored on posts) — derived from posts.Tags in posts. | users.Id AS Owner_Id: the owner's user id (aliased) — derived from users.Id via LEFT JOIN on users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId. | users.DisplayName AS Owner_DisplayName: the owner's display name (aliased) — derived from users.DisplayName via the same LEFT JOIN.
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.AnswerCount | posts.Title | posts.Tags | users.Id | users.DisplayName
params.metric: posts.Id = posts.Id  -- base key, not an aggregate (view is at row-level grain posts.Id) | posts.AnswerCount = posts.AnswerCount  -- passthrough metric: the stored column value from posts (no aggregation or transformation)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-user views/tables (for example users_core or users_basic_profile) on posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id — safe because users is one-row-per-user and this view is one-row-per-post, so joining preserves one row per post and does not duplicate post-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-post views/tables (for example posts_core or posts_minimal) on posts.Id = posts.Id — safe because both are one-row-per-post and will not duplicate measures if keys match 1:1. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables/views (for example user_badges, user_badges_by_user, user_post_counts if those are one-to-many or aggregated at a different grain) without re-aggregation on the result, because such joins will multiply rows for a post and thus duplicate post-level measures (AnswerCount, Title, etc.). If you need badge counts per post owner, aggregate badges to one-row-per-user first (e.g., user_badges_by_user) then join on OwnerUserId = users.Id. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join to tables that are many-to-many relative to posts (for example tag tables or comment tables with multiple rows per post) unless you first aggregate them to the post level (e.g., comment_count_by_post) to avoid inflating post measures. | composition recommendation: when composing metrics that sum or average post-level values (e.g., SUM(posts.AnswerCount)), perform those aggregations after any joins that may expand rows, or join only to aggregated summaries keyed to the same grain (posts.Id or users.Id aggregated appropriately) so the planner can preserve correct measure semantics.

views.name: posts_core_69
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.ViewCount, 0) AS ViewCount,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts p

params.description: Row-level normalized view of posts with basic identifying, ownership, view-count, title, type and creation date — one row per post Id.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic metadata for a single post or a set of posts (Id, owner, title, type, creation timestamp, view count). | Filter or select posts by OwnerUserId, PostTypeId, CreationDate, or Title and then compose further aggregations. | Join post-level data to user/person dimension rows (one-to-one or many-to-one from posts to users) without re-aggregating. | Build higher-level metrics by aggregating this view (e.g., counts of posts, sum/avg of ViewCount) as the starting point.
params.output_schema: Id: Post unique identifier — derived from posts.Id | OwnerUserId: Id of the user who owns/created the post — derived from posts.OwnerUserId | ViewCount: Number of times the post was viewed; NULLs normalized to 0 via COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0) — derived from posts.ViewCount with COALESCE | Title: Post title text — derived from posts.Title | PostTypeId: Numeric code for the post type (question, answer, etc.) — derived from posts.PostTypeId | CreationDate: Post creation timestamp — derived from posts.CreaionDate (as referenced in the view SQL)
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.ViewCount | posts.Title | posts.PostTypeId | posts.CreaionDate
params.metric: ViewCount = COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0)  -- a derived, non-aggregated column that replaces NULL with 0 for safe numeric use | No other aggregates are defined in this view; all other outputs are direct column projections.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a user dimension or single-row-per-user view (for example users_core or users_basic_profile) on posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id — safe because posts_core_69 is one-row-per-post and joining to one-row-per-user does not duplicate post-level rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_minimal or posts_core (other post-level NORM views) on Id = Id — safe because these are equivalently one-row-per-post, so measures remain 1:1. | do NOT directly join posts_core_69 to a one-to-many detail (for example user_badges or user_badges_by_user) on user keys without re-aggregation — such a join will duplicate post rows for each matching badge and multiply ViewCount and any derived aggregates computed after the join. | if you must combine post-level rows with one-to-many child rows (e.g., badges, comments, tags), first aggregate the child side to one row per post (or per OwnerUserId) preserving the intended measure (for example COUNT(tags) AS tag_count per post_id) and then join the aggregated result back to posts_core_69 — this prevents multiplication of post-level measures like ViewCount. | when deriving post-level aggregates (e.g., total views by owner), aggregate posts_core_69 (SUM(ViewCount) GROUP BY OwnerUserId) and then join to user-level views; do not SUM after joining raw one-to-many child tables because that will overcount unless the child side was pre-aggregated correctly. | joining to other post-level JOIN views (e.g., posts_with_owner_name, posts_with_owner) can be safe if those views are implemented as 1:1 enrichments; verify those sibling views do not introduce one-to-many expansions before composing, otherwise treat them like one-to-many children and re-aggregate appropriately.

views.name: author_post_views
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.OwnerUserId AS UserId,
  SUM(p.ViewCount) AS TotalViewCount,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS PostCount
FROM posts p
GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId

params.description: Per-user aggregates of posts: total view count across a user's posts and the number of posts they own.
params.when_to_use: Report the total number of post views for a specific user or set of users. | Rank or filter users by total post views or by how many posts they have. | Compose higher-level metrics about user activity that require per-user post counts or summed views. | Join to user profile information to present per-user view totals alongside profile fields (one-to-one joins).
params.output_schema: UserId: the OwnerUserId from the posts table; identifies the owner of the aggregated posts (derived from posts.OwnerUserId). | TotalViewCount: the sum of ViewCount for all posts owned by that user (derived from SUM(posts.ViewCount)). | PostCount: the count of posts (rows) owned by that user (derived from COUNT(posts.Id)).
params.grounded_columns: posts.OwnerUserId | posts.ViewCount | posts.Id
params.metric: TotalViewCount = SUM(posts.ViewCount) -- sum of the base ViewCount column over posts grouped by posts.OwnerUserId | PostCount = COUNT(posts.Id) -- count of post rows per posts.OwnerUserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a user-level (one-row-per-user) view/table such as users_basic_profile, users_core, or users_core_6 on users.id = author_post_views.UserId — safe because author_post_views is one-row-per-UserId, so joining to another one-row-per-user source does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (if that sibling view is also one-row-per-owner) on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = author_post_views.UserId — safe only if posts_by_owner is guaranteed one-row-per-owner (it must not be a detailed/post-level view). | DO NOT join directly to post-level tables or views that are one-to-many from users (for example posts_row_level, posts_core, posts_minimal, posts_with_owner, posts_with_owner_name) without re-aggregation — joining author_post_views to those will multiply the aggregated measures (TotalViewCount and PostCount) because those sources contain multiple rows per UserId. | DO NOT join to user_badges (if it is one-row-per-badge) or user_badges_by_user (if it is one-row-per-badge) without ensuring those are pre-aggregated to one row per user; otherwise badge-level rows will multiply measures. If you need badge attributes, either (a) aggregate badges to one row per user before joining, or (b) join to badge data at query time and re-aggregate TotalViewCount and PostCount after the join. | If composing further aggregates (for example computing average views per post across a set of users or summing TotalViewCount across users), operate on author_post_views' PostCount and TotalViewCount directly (e.g., SUM(TotalViewCount) or SUM(TotalViewCount)/SUM(PostCount)) — this preserves correctness because author_post_views has one row per UserId. | When joining to any dimension or lookup that is many-to-one into the user (for example a single canonical profile row per user), it is safe and does not require re-aggregation. When joining to any many-side relation keyed by UserId, either pre-aggregate that relation to one row per UserId or perform the join as a subquery and re-aggregate after the join to avoid measure duplication.
